fields.data_definition: Official website of the project or the managing entity’s or developing company’s page where they have information about the project.
Official logo of the project or the managing entity’s if there’s none available for the project itself.
Self-description of the project’s goal/mission from an official source.
The date the project was first publicly announced. If no official announcement was made, the date of the company's founding year will be used.

If applicable, the date the first deliverable/product went live.
The date can also refer to when the project first launched its beta version or a pilot version.

Status could be:
1. Announced: It has been publicly stated that the project is going to be developed.
2. Pilot: currently in testing stages before being publicly launched more widely.
3. Launched: it is already active and working.
4. Discontinued: project was declared discontinued publicly.

Any government or state-affiliated entity that has an affiliation at a national, regional, municipal, or international level with the consortium through endorsement.

Endorsement is defined as statements of support, adoption, funding, partnerships, formal recommendations, branding, certifications or awards, or resource allocation. These entities can be government agencies or institutions, state-owned enterprises, intergovernmental organizations, regional alliances, etc.

fields.data_definition:
Indicates the amount of data available for the project regarding DLT.
1. Complete DLT Data: the project provides public information about the technology or instance used.
2. Specifies DLT Technology but no DLT Instance: the project publicly states the use of Hyperledger, Tendermint, or R3 Corda, but does not specify which instance.
3. Uses DLT, no specifications: the project publicly states the use of DLT for the project, but does not specify any technology or instance.
4. No DLT data at all: the project does not publicly state whether they use DLT.

Whether the project explicitly mentions the holder can export their credentials.
If the project mentions it can only import and doesn’t specify they can be exported “No” will be used. If no information about import/export is identified “Failed to disclose” will be used

The project explicitly mentions the holder has exclusive custody of the credentials and keys. “Failed to disclose” will be used whenever there is no information about the storage of credentials and
